lines.say: a pegylated copy of an IGF-1 tail peptide; never studied in people
not shown to exist on its own in the body or to do more than full-length IGF-1
its case rests on unmodified MGF in cells and rodents, with conflicting results
MGF peptide didn't grow muscle cells in a 2014 lab study, while mature IGF-1 did
nerve cells protected after brain ischemia in gerbils (animal studies)
heart function improved in mice, from gel rods placed in the heart (mouse study)
FDA flagged immune reactions to the peptide as a possible significant risk

ask: Is there any human evidence that PEG-MGF builds muscle or speeds healing?
